pharm: Inhibits SGLT2 in the proximal renal tubule, lowering the renal threshold for glucose and increasing urinary glucose excretion, which lowers blood glucose insulin-independently.
quick: 100 mg once daily before the first meal; may increase to 300 mg once daily
Take before the first meal of the day
Not recommended in 2nd/3rd trimesters (fetal renal effects)
eGFR 30-<60: max 100 mg; eGFR <30: do not initiate (may continue 100 mg if albuminuria)
No adjustment mild-moderate; not recommended in severe
Excess alcohol increases DKA and hypoglycemia risk
Renal function, volume status, ketones if symptoms, foot exams
summary: Canagliflozin is an SGLT2 inhibitor that lowers blood glucose by promoting urinary glucose excretion independent of insulin, and also reduces major adverse cardiovascular events and slows progression of diabetic kidney disease in eligible patients. It carries important risks: diabetic ketoacidosis (which can occur with near-normal glucose), genital mycotic infections, volume depletion and acute kidney injury, increased risk of lower-limb amputation, and bone fracture. It is taken once daily before the first meal. Dosing is capped at 100 mg in moderate renal impairment, and initiation is not recommended once eGFR falls below 30. Hypoglycemia is uncommon alone but more likely with insulin or sulfonylureas.
indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease

Reduction of risk of end-stage kidney disease, doubling of serum creatinine, cardiovascular death, and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with type 2 diabetes and diabetic nephropathy with albuminuria

dosage.d: 100 mg once daily before the first meal of the day
May increase to 300 mg once daily if eGFR >=60 and additional control needed
Initiation not recommended; patients with albuminuria >300 mg/day may continue 100 mg once daily for cardiorenal benefit

admin: Take orally once daily before the first meal of the day
Assess volume status and correct hypovolemia before starting, especially in the elderly or those on diuretics
Check renal function before initiation and periodically thereafter
Consider temporarily withholding during acute illness, fasting, surgery, or reduced intake (ketoacidosis risk)
Examine feet regularly and treat foot infections/ulcers promptly given amputation risk
moa: Canagliflozin selectively and reversibly inhibits sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) in the S1 segment of the renal proximal tubule, which is responsible for the majority of filtered glucose reabsorption. By blocking SGLT2, it lowers the renal threshold for glucose and increases urinary glucose excretion, reducing plasma glucose in an insulin-independent manner. The accompanying osmotic diuresis and natriuresis contribute to modest reductions in blood pressure and weight and underlie the cardiovascular and renal protective effects, while the loss of glucose calories and intratubular effects mediate metabolic and hemodynamic kidney benefits.

absolute: History of serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis, angioedema) to canagliflozin
Severe renal impairment, end-stage renal disease, or dialysis (for glycemic indication)
relative: Type 1 diabetes (increased ketoacidosis risk; not recommended)
Volume depletion, hypotension, or treatment with loop diuretics
History of lower-limb amputation, peripheral vascular disease, neuropathy, or diabetic foot ulcers
Conditions predisposing to ketoacidosis (low carbohydrate intake, alcohol abuse, pancreatic insufficiency)
Recurrent genital mycotic or urinary tract infections
monitor: Renal function (eGFR) before and during therapy
Signs of ketoacidosis (even with near-normal glucose)

preg: Use is not recommended during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy; animal studies showed adverse renal effects (renal pelvic and tubular dilatation) during the period corresponding to the second and third trimesters of human pregnancy.
lact: Canagliflozin is not recommended while breastfeeding because of the potential for adverse effects on the developing kidney; the maturing human kidney undergoes development through about 2 years of age.
renal: Efficacy depends on renal function. For glycemic control, use 100-300 mg if eGFR >=60; limit to 100 mg if eGFR 30-<60; do not initiate if eGFR <30. Patients with diabetic nephropathy and albuminuria >300 mg/day may continue 100 mg once daily for cardiorenal benefit per label. Increases risk of volume depletion and acute kidney injury.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed in mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B). Use is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), as it has not been studied.

major: Insulin and insulin secretagogues (sulfonylureas) - increased hypoglycemia risk; consider lowering their dose
moderate: UGT enzyme inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, phenobarbital, ritonavir) - reduce canagliflozin exposure; consider increasing to 300 mg if eGFR >=60
Digoxin - canagliflozin increases digoxin exposure; monitor
Lithium - canagliflozin may decrease serum lithium; monitor levels
interactions.food: Take before the first meal of the day; food does not clinically affect exposure but pre-meal dosing improves postprandial control.
interactions.alcohol: Excessive alcohol or binge drinking increases the risk of ketoacidosis and hypoglycemia; advise moderation.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes positive urine glucose tests and makes the 1,5-anhydroglucitol (1,5-AG) assay unreliable for monitoring glycemia; use HbA1c or plasma glucose instead.

serious: Diabetic ketoacidosis (may occur with near-normal glucose)
Volume depletion and acute kidney injury
rare: Necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier gangrene)

monitoring: Renal function (eGFR) at baseline and periodically
Signs/symptoms of ketoacidosis regardless of glucose level
Lower-limb examination for ulcers, infection, and circulation
HbA1c for glycemic response (not urine glucose)
counsel: Take one tablet each morning before your first meal
Seek urgent care for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, tiredness, or trouble breathing - this can be ketoacidosis even if your sugar is not very high
Drink adequate fluids; lightheadedness on standing may mean you are dehydrated
Genital yeast infections and urinary infections are common - report itching, discharge, or burning
Check your feet daily and tell your doctor about any sores, redness, or new pain
Tell your doctor before any surgery or if you become unwell and cannot eat or drink normally
pk: Glucose-lowering begins within the first day; effect maintained with daily dosing
Plasma Tmax ~1-2 hours after oral dosing
Once-daily dosing; steady state in 4-5 days
pearls: DKA can occur with near-normal glucose (euglycemic DKA) - check ketones if symptomatic, not just glucose
Hold during acute illness, fasting, dehydration, or before major surgery (sick-day rules)
Increased risk of lower-limb amputation and bone fracture - examine feet, assess fracture risk
Genital mycotic infections (and rarely Fournier gangrene) are class effects - counsel on perineal symptoms
Provides cardiovascular and renal protection beyond glucose lowering in eligible patients
Reduce insulin/sulfonylurea dose to limit hypoglycemia; little hypoglycemia when used alone
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next day's dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is limited experience with overdose. Management is supportive based on the patient's clinical status, including correcting volume depletion and electrolyte abnormalities and monitoring for ketoacidosis. Hemodialysis is not expected to remove canagliflozin effectively, and peritoneal dialysis is also not expected to be effective.
